g11-economics-ue4-t1.overview: Consumption sits inside Consumption, Saving and Investment. Consumption and saving are the focus of Unit 4 of Grade 11 Economics in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it studies consumption, the average and marginal propensity to consume, and what determines them. Then it studies saving, the average and marginal propensity to save, and its determinants. Next, it links saving to consumption. Finally, it examines investment, its types, and its role in economic growth. Students will also learn how consumption and saving shape real-life economic activity.
objectives: Compute the average and marginal propensity to consume.
Compute the average and marginal propensity to save.
Explain the determinants of consumption and saving.
Describe the types and determinants of investment.
Explain how consumption and saving relate to investment.
g11-economics-ue4-t1.simple:
Consumption in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, the average propensity to consume (APC = C/Y).
  • Then the marginal propensity to consume (MPC = ΔC/ΔY).
  • Also the determinants of consumption expenditure.
g11-economics-ue4-t1.detailed:
Consumption — the essentials. First, the average propensity to consume (APC = C/Y). Then the marginal propensity to consume (MPC = ΔC/ΔY). Also the determinants of consumption expenditure.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Compute the average and marginal propensity to consume.
  • Compute the average and marginal propensity to save.
  • Explain the determinants of consumption and saving.
  • Describe the types and determinants of investment.
  • Explain how consumption and saving relate to investment.
